name: Slider

knownIssues.summary: A pointer press on a disabled single Slider still sets `data-dragging="true"`; the disabled styles hide it.
Its examples file uses a `type` prop that doesn't exist (`<Slider type="slider-range">`).
The hover-only value bubble floats over the label.
No `invalid` state or message, and Field's page doesn't list it among the controls it wires.

figmaSource.note: This component's type prop selects between three separate Figma components, not one - each recorded separately below.

behaviorRules: Inside a disabled <fieldset>, the native control is disabled without the disabled prop, and the component looks and behaves exactly as with disabled (its disabled styling also keys off :disabled, via :has() on the wrapper).
SliderRange submits the lower value under minName and the upper under maxName; they default to name and `${name}Max`.
showValue keeps the value bubble showing and makes room for it above the track, so it never overlaps the label.
SliderRange is a group named by label, aria-labelledby, or aria-label; each handle's name is that name plus minLabel or maxLabel.
implementationNotes: Shared FocusRing, drawn on the visible handle from the primitive's variables (the native input fills the control and has no outline)
